plot: At dawn on moving day the lunchbox slides off Dad's car roof onto the wet lawn and the family drives away, so the Dough Bros must cross the lawn to Grandma's red car before she leaves, but it starts raining and every drop dims Crispy's embers; they dodge movers' boots under the ramp, a leaf umbrella fails, Grandma comes out early, and — the twist — Bup uses the one thing stale bread is great at, soaking up water, riding on top of Crispy as a bread roof so Crispy glows again; they leap into Grandma's knitting bag, she dries soggy Bup on the heater, and her phone starts the route to Grandma's house, three hours the wrong way.

script.title: Dad Drove Off With Us on the Roof

beats.say: Hold on! Everybody hold on to something!
There's nothing to hold! It's a lunchbox!
Dawn. Moving day. Dad drives off with the lunchbox on the roof.
At the corner it slides off. Thump. Onto the wet lawn.
New episode every day. Subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
The car is gone. Mia is gone. Everybody's gone!
Not everybody. Grandma follows at seven. In her own car.
Grandma's little red car waits at the far end of the lawn.
Then we cross the lawn. Easy. Thirty steps.
Not easy. The grass is soaked. Then it starts to rain.
Rain. Of course. My one weakness.
Every drop that hits Crispy hisses. His glow gets a little darker.
If Crispy g-goes out, does he come back on?
I don't know. I've never been out.
Okay team. We run under things. We stay dry.
They run under the movers' ramp. Huge boots thump above them.
Movers carry the couch. Then the beds. Then Mom's plants.
Boot! Left! Boot! Right! Another boot!
A boot lands one inch from Pim. Pim faints flat.
Pick him up! Fainted beans still count!
I'm awake! I'm awake! Was that a boot?!
At the end of the ramp there's only open grass. And rain.
Twenty steps of rain. I won't make it. I'm sure.
We came off that roof together. We cross together.
Zeek holds a leaf over Crispy. The rain pours straight through.
Leaves are terrible umbrellas. I'll write a strongly worded paper.
Then Grandma's front door opens. Car keys jingle.
She's early! Grandma is never early! Never!
Crispy is barely glowing now. One small orange dot.
Crispy, stay on. Please. You're our night-light.
Bup looks at the rain. Then at himself. Old. Dry. Hard.
Stale bread drinks water. It's the one thing I'm great at.
Bup climbs on top of Crispy, like a little bread roof.
Bup. You'll get soggy. You'll never be crusty again.
Crusty is totally overrated. Everybody, run! Now!
They run. The rain hits Bup. Bup drinks every drop.
Under him, Crispy stays dry. His embers glow bright orange again.
Grandma opens the back door to put in her knitting bag.
Now! Jump now! Into the knitting bag!
Five Dough Bros leap into the bag. Plop. Plop. Squish.
Grandma looks down. Five little faces. One very soggy loaf.
She tuts, and sets the soggy one on the warm heater vent.
Oh. Oh, that's nice. That's very, very nice.
You drank the rain for me. I won't forget that.
You'd do it for me. Slowly. But you would.
All five. In a car. Going to the new house!
Grandma taps her phone. A calm voice speaks.
'Starting route. To: Grandma's house. Three hours.'
Grandma's house? That's the completely wrong way!
What do you think happens in the next part?
Tell me in the comments.
